h1:
Phrae on a Budget
3 Days 2 Nights Backpacker Style
intro: Phrae is a small city that punches well above its weight for budget travelers. Guesthouses start at a few hundred THB, many attractions are free or cost next to nothing, and a plate of local food runs 40–60 THB. This 3-day, 2-night plan covers the old town on foot, gets you out to the main highlights by rented motorbike, and works perfectly well without a private car.
chips: 💸 Budget stays from a few hundred THB

blocks.html: What makes Phrae so good for budget travelers is how compact it is. The old town's top draws — Kham Chao Luang mansion, Baan Wongburi, and several historic temples — all sit within a few kilometers of each other. The farther spots, Wat Phra That Cho Hae and Phae Mueang Phi, are easy day-trip rides by rented motorbike. This plan keeps costs to around 1,500–2,000 THB per person (bus fare not included). Share a room with a friend and it gets cheaper still.

blocks.text: Getting to Phrae on the Cheap

blocks.html: The cheapest option is an overnight bus from Bangkok's Mo Chit terminal — about 8 hours, tickets around 470–550 THB. Operators include Pornpiritour, Bussarakam Tour, Sombat Tour, and BKSP 999. Most depart in the evening and arrive in the morning, which saves you one night's accommodation. From Phrae's bus terminal, hop on a songthaew or motorbike taxi into the old town.

blocks.title: Book Your Bus Ticket in Advance
blocks.html: Buses fill up fast on long weekends. Book online through sites like busonlineticket or busx to secure your seat — prices are sometimes lower than buying at the counter.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Phrae trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

blocks.html: The old town area has several friendly hostels and guesthouses. Dorm beds run a few hundred THB per night; private rooms start a bit higher. Staying inside the old town keeps transport costs down since most sights are walkable.

items.name: Need A Nap Hostel Phrae
items.blurb: A clean, airy minimalist hostel with dorms and private rooms, a shared kitchen, a café, and parking. Smack in the old town — step out the door and you are already sightseeing.

items.name: I-Sabai@Jomsuwan Hostel
items.blurb: A no-frills daily-rate guesthouse in town at a very low price — solid pick for budget travelers who just need a clean bed near the sights.

items.name: Phrae Nakara Hotel
items.blurb: A small affordable hotel with private rooms starting in the lower hundreds. Good if you want your own room without paying boutique prices.

blocks.html: Prices shown are starting rates visible on booking sites at time of writing — they can shift with the season and holidays. Compare on Agoda and Trip.com before booking, and check real guest reviews for cleanliness and location.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Old Town Walking Day — Almost Free

items.activity: Check in (or drop your bag) at the guesthouse, then walk into the old town.
items.note: If you arrive early on an overnight bus, most places will hold your bags before official check-in time.

items.activity: Start at Kham Chao Luang — a Thai-European teak mansion famous for its story and 72 doors.
items.note: Open 08:30–16:30. Small entry fee of a few tens of THB — well worth it for the photos.

items.activity: Walk over to Baan Wongburi, a pink century-old heritage house with guided history talks.
items.note: Entry around 30 THB. Open 09:00–17:00.

items.activity: Lunch at a famous khao soi nam ngiao stall near the municipal market — been running for over 40 years.
items.note: 40–60 THB a bowl, proper Northern Thai flavor. Grab some crispy pork skin on the side.

items.activity: Stroll the old town streets past teak houses, then swing by Wat Phra Bat Ming Mueang and Wat Jom Sawan.
items.note: Most temples are free to enter — donate what you like.

items.activity: If it is a Saturday night, the Gad Sam Wai walking street is on — great cheap street food.
items.note: Snacks from 10–20 THB each. You can eat your fill for under 100 THB.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Rent a Motorbike — Cho Hae Temple and Phae Mueang Phi

items.activity: Pick up a motorbike rental in town, fill up the tank, and head out to Wat Phra That Cho Hae — about 9 km from the center.
items.note: A day's rental costs a few hundred THB. Much cheaper than hiring a driver.

items.activity: Pay respects at Wat Phra That Cho Hae, Phrae's patron temple — an eight-sided Chiang Saen-style chedi.
items.note: Open 09:00–16:30. No entry fee. Locals say this is the one temple you must visit in Phrae.

items.activity: Find lunch on the way back — try khao soi hor or old-school tom yum noodles. Cheap and filling.
items.note: 50–70 THB a bowl.

items.activity: Ride out to Phae Mueang Phi forest park to see the dramatic soil pillars and eroded rock formations.
items.note: Small entry fee of a few tens of THB. About an hour to walk around. Still off most tourists' radars — great for photos.

items.activity: Ride back to town, return the bike, and stop at a teak-house café for a coffee.
items.note: Local café coffee runs 50–70 THB — nice atmosphere to rest your legs.

items.activity: Dinner at the Pratu Chai night market — night-shift khao soi nam ngiao plus all kinds of local snacks.
items.note: Eat well for under a few hundred THB.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Light Souvenir Shopping Before Heading Home

items.activity: Simple breakfast near your guesthouse, then browse the Phrae morning market.
items.note: Breakfast dishes from 30–40 THB.

items.activity: Head to the Baan Thung Hong neighborhood to check out mor hom (indigo-dyed) fabric — Phrae's signature souvenir. Pick something small and affordable.
items.note: Mor hom handkerchiefs and shirts come in a range of prices to suit any budget.

items.activity: Last meal out, then grab some khao kaeb or crispy pork rinds to take home.
items.note: Dry snack souvenirs are inexpensive and easy to pack.

items.activity: Head to Phrae bus terminal for your bus back.
items.note: Book your return ticket in advance for peace of mind.

blocks.text: Getting Around Town Without Spending Much

items: On foot — the old town is very walkable. Kham Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi, and the historic temples are all close together, so you barely need to spend on transport.
Rented motorbike — a few hundred THB per day. The best option if you're heading out to Cho Hae and Phae Mueang Phi. Easy riding, low traffic.
Songthaew (shared truck) — runs around town and to the bus terminal. Ask your guesthouse about stops and fares.
Motorbike taxi — available at the bus terminal. Handy when you have bags or need to reach somewhere the songthaews don't cover.

blocks.html: Here's a rough 3-day, 2-night breakdown (bus fare to/from Bangkok of around 940–1,100 THB not included): accommodation for 2 nights runs roughly 1,000–1,400 THB (half that if you share a room); food comes to about 200–300 THB per day; motorbike rental plus petrol for one day is around 300–400 THB; all entrance fees combined are under 100 THB; add a little for small souvenirs. Total: a 3-day Phrae trip is very doable at 1,500–2,000 THB per person.

blocks.title: Squeeze the Budget Further
blocks.html: The two biggest savers are sleeping in a hostel dorm and splitting the motorbike rental with a friend. Food in Phrae is already cheap — no need to skimp on that.

faq.q: How much money do I need for 3 days in Phrae?
faq.a: Staying in a hostel dorm, eating local food, and renting a motorbike for one day, you can get through 3 days and 2 nights on about 1,500–2,000 THB per person. That does not include the bus from Bangkok and back, which adds roughly 940–1,100 THB. Share a room and it drops further.

faq.q: Can I visit Phrae without a private car?
faq.a: Easily. The old town is completely walkable, and the farther spots — Wat Phra That Cho Hae and Phae Mueang Phi — are reachable in one day on a rented motorbike costing a few hundred THB. Songthaews and motorbike taxis fill in the gaps.

faq.q: Where can I find cheap accommodation in Phrae?
faq.a: Several hostels and guesthouses are in town. Need A Nap Hostel starts at around ฿689; I-Sabai@Jomsuwan Hostel has rooms under ฿500; and Phrae Nakara Hotel has private rooms from around ฿570. Compare on Agoda and Trip.com before booking.

faq.q: Which sights in Phrae are free to enter?
faq.a: Wat Phra That Cho Hae has no entry fee. Most historic temples in the old town are free to enter. Walking the teak-house streets and the night walking street costs nothing. Kham Chao Luang, Baan Wongburi, and Phae Mueang Phi charge small fees of a few tens of THB each.

faq.q: How much is the bus from Bangkok to Phrae?
faq.a: Tickets run around 468–550 THB one way. Operators include Pornpiritour, Bussarakam Tour, Sombat Tour, and BKSP 999. The journey takes about 8 hours. Taking an overnight bus saves you one night's accommodation.
